---
name: orchestrated-refactor
description: "Orchestrate a large refactor across files or sessions: scope slices, dispatch model-matched workers in owned worktrees, review, integrate and maintain a tracked handoff. Use for explicit delegated implementation; ordinary one-session changes use the normal branch/PR workflow."
---

# Orchestrated Refactor

Portable Claude Code skill: copy this folder into `<repo>/.claude/skills/` or `~/.claude/skills/`; never over a same-named skill another installer manages. It assumes git and Claude Code; every other tool is detected at run start and used only when present.

The main session only scopes, dispatches, reviews, commits Codex slices, integrates, merges and hands off; workers implement slices. The repo's own CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rules bind every worker; carry the essentials in its prompt.

`<root>` is the absolute primary checkout; `<run-id>` is `<slug>-<6 random hex>`, recorded once and reused. Manual worktrees: `<root>/.tmp/worktrees/<run-id>-<slice-id>`. `<state>`: `<root>/.tmp/orchestrated-refactor/<run-id>/<slice-id>/`; an isolated worker's state lives inside its worktree at `.tmp/orchestrated-refactor/<run-id>/<slice-id>/`. Record resolved paths. Slice ids are never `review`. Shell commands here are bash; in PowerShell use 7.4+ (older versions re-encode `>` output). If `.tmp/` is not ignored, append `.tmp/` to `$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)/info/exclude` (local, covers every worktree, no commit); operational state is ignored, the run handoff is tracked.

## Qualify

Use only for refactors spanning many files/projects or sessions, or explicit delegated implementation. Work that fits one session uses the normal workflow.

## Phase 0 - Environment detect

Run once per session before any edit; record results in the handoff's Environment table when Phase 1 creates it. Later sections apply an optional tool only when it was detected here.

| Check | Command / marker | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | `codex --version`, `codex login status` | Cross-family review lens and optional workers |
| RTK | `rtk --version`; an `rtk` PreToolUse hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings*.json` | Worker TOOLING line |
| Graphify | `graphify-out/graph.json` exists and `graphify` on PATH; may be stale, so confirm graph answers against the code | One scoping query |
| GitHub CLI | `gh auth status` | PR creation, CI status |
| Default branch | `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` (strip `origin/`); if unset, `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name` or `git remote set-head origin --auto` and retry | Worktree base, PR target |
| MCP servers | `claude mcp list` (starts configured servers, including repo-defined ones; run only in a repo you trust) | Tooling line per slice |
| Toolchain | SDK pins, lockfiles, package engines, test runners, Compose files | Slice GATE commands |
| Platform | OS and shell | Worktree serialization, command syntax |

Report required but absent tools with the exact install command and what they unblock. Install nothing and change no global config without the user's yes.

## Phase 1 - Scope (orchestrator)

1. If Graphify was detected, query it once for the affected area; otherwise use targeted search.
2. Design before slicing when the work will take more than one slice and those slices would share a lifecycle or need one shared mechanism, or when it touches money, security, data lifecycle or concurrency; a handed `full-review` plan is exempt: its slices, order, approval marks and shared-mechanism contracts are taken as written, never redesigned here, and each row records its reviewed SHA, evidence paths and, once merged, its commit SHAs (step 5). At adoption, before each slice dispatches and again before it merges, after a fetch, `git log --oneline <reviewed-sha>..origin/<default> -- <SCOPE and evidence paths>`, ignoring the `full-review` report and its amendment commits, this run's handoff commits and the commits of the plan's merged slices ordered before it, must be empty. Otherwise stop all further plan dispatch (queued slices stay queued and the stop is the recorded next action; in-flight slices finish, each checked before merge) and give the slice to the user, who drops it (every live slice ordered after it then goes to the user too), accepts it unchanged (its row records the current default head as reviewed SHA) or starts a `full-review` re-run whose plan replaces every live unmerged row; dispatch resumes only when no slice awaits that choice and no re-run is pending. A dropped row stays in the table as `dropped by the user`, a replaced one as superseded; a stopped, dropped or replaced row keeps its branch, PR and worktree until the user decides about them. An approval-marked slice, and one accepted unchanged, dispatches only after the user's yes. Write a tracked design record (repo convention, else `docs/plans/<slug>-design.md`, linked from the handoff):
   - one state machine or pure decision type per lifecycle, with numbered rules (states, transitions, guards, outcomes);
   - one contract per shared mechanism the work needs: lock order, idempotency-key scheme, outbound-provider-call protocol (such as receipt before call), failure classification and error codes, handler outcome types, sweep runner, notification/alert/audit/timeline path, cache invalidation. Each names its one implementation, its callers and how a new caller joins, and is marked as follows (one mechanism per job). Mark each mechanism a change needs reuse, extend or new, in that order of preference: reuse where the repo has exactly one implementation for that job and it fits; extend where that one falls short or two or more exist (consolidate them into one, even when one already fits); new only where none exists or extending cannot meet the need. A consolidation or replacement records why, names every implementation it retires, and the mechanism slice that extends or builds the surviving one, together with any slices a split move continues in, moves every caller to it, the last of them deleting the retired ones, except a reader that persisted or in-flight data still needs, kept with its removal condition (global Data rule).

   Before any slice dispatches, a fresh-context design lens (Review path opus Claude reviewer form, else the Codex form; never the authoring conversation; with neither, it goes to the user like an open finding below) reads the goal, the record and the code it touches, and reports missing lifecycles or mechanisms, a rule or mechanism defined twice, a contract whose mark is missing or wrong against the marks defined above and the repo's existing mechanisms, a retirement whose recorded reason does not hold or that misses an existing implementation or caller, and contracts that conflict or that a slice would have to bypass. Fix or rebut each finding; a changed contract gets one more lens pass; a finding still open after it goes to the user before dispatch (an unattended run applies its caller's needs-human signal and stops). Record lens, model and verdict in the handoff.
3. Slice by explicit paths, spec and runnable finish line, leaving context reserve for tool output and edits. Each slice owns a branch; serialize dependencies and parallelize independent work. Split anything that needs the reserve to fit. Slice by mechanism as well as feature: when the design record names a shared mechanism, slice 0 extends the mechanisms marked extend, builds those marked new (never a second implementation beside one the repo keeps) and adds one end-to-end path through every mechanism the record names (split into mechanism slices in dependency order when that, or a caller move, exceeds one slice's reserve: the first also adds the tests the repo lacks for reused ones, each one's architecture tests cover the mechanisms built, extended or reused so far, a caller move may continue in the next (each slice of it leaves both implementations working, and the one-implementation assertion for that mechanism lands in the slice that completes the move and retirement; a mid-move slice that stops or is dropped goes to the user with the two-implementation state named), the last adds the end-to-end path, and all are ordered before the slices that use them), with architecture tests (the repo's existing tool, else plain tests in its framework) asserting one implementation per mechanism, reused ones included (a kept reader the design record lists with its removal condition is excluded until that condition is met), and one caller per wrapped gateway or IO entry point. When every contract is marked reuse, slice 0 only adds what the repo lacks of those architecture tests and of a passing end-to-end path through the mechanisms, and there is no slice 0 when it lacks neither; a mechanism added later (Feedback loop) gets its own mechanism slice when it needs one, held to the same tests, which moves any caller of a parallel path to it. Feature slices depend on the mechanism slices they use and own no mechanism. Plan the PRs per Integrate and merge (ship in increments).
4. At open behavior choices, prefer entity/target-scoped configuration or data policy when it needs no significant redesign; record the policy shape in SCOPE. Where an `engineering-criteria` skill or copy is available, carry Principles (Design) into SCOPE and the sections a slice touches into its SCOPE and DONE: Tests for any logic change; Scale for data access, outbound calls, background work or shared state; Documentation for public API; Operations for logging, retention or deploy scripts. Without one, each slice builds the right design even when it costs more than a narrow patch: it removes the duplication it touches (reuse or extract a shared helper), keeps one decision point per rule (for example one state machine instead of status checks spread across handlers) and keeps one mechanism per job, reusing or extending the repo's existing one before building one (for example one idempotency-key builder every handler uses instead of each formatting its own), without over-engineering. Either way, each slice carries the design record's contracts and decision types it uses into SCOPE.
5. Create the tracked handoff (repo convention, else `docs/plans/<slug>-refactor.md`): run id, goal, design record link and lens verdict (step 2), decisions, Environment table, next action, active count, FIFO queue and slice table. Each row records scope, weight, family/model/substitutions, status, branch/PR, worktree, worker/thread id and state path, plus, for a handed `full-review` slice, its reviewed SHA, evidence paths and, once merged, its commit SHAs.

## Model assignment

Routing as of 2026-10; re-check vendor docs and coding benchmarks when a new model ships. Missing evidence is not endorsement.

| Model | Route here | Never route here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| haiku | Extraction, inventory/verification sweeps and doc-only work with explicit paths and cheaply checked results | Coding or large-input recall |
| sonnet | Clear-spec implementation, mechanical multi-file changes, tests with a runnable check; precision-first review | Unmeasured recall-first, long-horizon or toolchain work |
| opus | Hard cross-file/architecture/long-horizon coding; build/dependency/toolchain work; recall-first review | - |
| fable | Reasoning escalation after opus fails; security review | Build, dependency, packaging, toolchain; exploits or attack tooling |
| codex (if detected) | Fat independent coding/test slices with paths, spec and runnable check; cross-family review | Small/correction-heavy slices, or context that cannot be carried in the prompt |
| main session | Scope, dispatch, review, Codex slice commits, integration, merge, handoff | Slice implementation |

Pass family aliases (`haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`, `fable`), never dated model ids or model-default env overrides. Record the model that actually served each slice. Review never uses a model banned for the subject.

Availability fallback: fable -> opus; opus -> sonnet with a smaller scope; haiku -> sonnet; sonnet -> opus. Record substitutions. Never cross a subject ban; if none is eligible, ask.

## Recommended settings

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Orchestrator | opus, `/effort high`; consider a larger autocompact window for long runs and record it in the handoff |
| Workers | Inherit effort unless overridden; use per-call `effort: "high"` when the session runs at xhigh or max and announce it |
| Codex | Newest listed `gpt-<version>-sol` from `codex debug models` (highest version with `visibility: list`) for workers and review, resolved before every worker launch and review lens; a resume keeps its session's model (if no sol model is listed, use the strongest listed non-astra model and record the substitution); explicit `-m` on exec, explicit `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>` and `-c model_auto_compact_token_limit=230000 -c model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope=total` on every exec/resume (keeps input under the 272K price band). Never `astra` or `ultra` |

## Delegation mechanics

Implementation: `Agent`, `subagent_type: general-purpose`, family `model`, `isolation: "worktree"`, background by default. Search sweeps may use Explore without isolation.

Isolated agents cannot write outside their worktree. When a slice needs that (or the shell hook refuses isolated git), use a non-isolated agent restricted by prompt to a manual worktree. Run `git fetch origin` first, then `git worktree add "<root>/.tmp/worktrees/<run-id>-<slice-id>" -b <type>/<run-id>-<slice-id> origin/<default-branch>`, where `<type>` is `feature`, `fix`, `chore` or `docs`.

On Windows serialize worktree creation, including harness-managed spawns (at most one isolation spawn per message). Before dispatch create manual `<state>` or pass the isolated worker a state path relative to its worktree.

Codex worker (only if detected and logged in): create the manual worktree and `<state>`, resolve the model (Recommended settings), then run in background from bash (every Codex form here; PowerShell 7.3+: pipe `@() |` instead of `< /dev/null` and read prompt files as below):

`codex exec --json -s workspace-write -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort=<medium|high> -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=230000 -c model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope=total -C "<worktree>" --add-dir "<state>" --output-last-message "<state>/report.md" "$(cat "<state>/prompt.md")" < /dev/null > "<state>/log.jsonl"`

Write each prompt or correction to a file at an absolute path and pass its contents, never inline text: bash `"$(cat "<file>")"`, PowerShell 7.3+ `(Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath "<file>")` (plain `cat` there joins lines with spaces). Double-quoted inline text is expanded by the shell (`$(...)` and backticks in bash, `$var` and `$(...)` in PowerShell), so quoted PR, issue or diff text could run commands. Quote every path.

Effort: medium for clear-spec slices, high for cross-file work. Record the thread id from the first `thread.started` event; never read the full JSONL. Correct from `<worktree>` (resume has no `-C` or `-s`): `codex exec resume --json -c sandbox_mode=workspace-write -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["<state>"]' -c model_reasoning_effort=<level> -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=230000 -c model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope=total --output-last-message "<state>/report.md" <thread-id> "$(cat "<state>/correction.md")" < /dev/null >> "<state>/log.jsonl"`; the session keeps its model. Use forward slashes in `<state>` inside that TOML value. The sandbox cannot write a linked worktree's git metadata, so Codex workers do not commit: their BRANCH line says "leave changes uncommitted", and the orchestrator commits in `<worktree>` after reviewing the diff. The orchestrator commits (`git -C "<worktree>" add -A` after checking `git status` for stray files, then `git commit`) after each reviewed report, before each resume and before abandoning or respawning a stopped worker, so a lost worktree or replacement worker starts from that commit. This overrides any repo rule telling workers to commit. Network is off and writes outside `<worktree>`/`<state>` fail (package caches, SDK first-run state, browser installs): restore/prepare in `<worktree>` before dispatch, or keep such slices on Claude workers. The sandbox still reads anything the user can: trusted slices only.

## Worker prompt template

Adapt this into every prompt, including cold replacement workers:

```
SCOPE: <paths, change, explicit non-goals and chosen policy shape>
DONE: <runnable finish line>
CONTRACTS: <design record path and the contracts and decision types this slice uses, verbatim, or a handed `full-review` plan's shared-mechanism contracts; "none" when neither exists>. Use these and the mechanisms the repo already has; never add a parallel one (another lock, key format, notification path, cache eviction or outcome type). If the slice needs a shared mechanism, or a rule another slice also decides, that neither provides, stop and report "needs contract: <what, why>"; never invent one. Rules local to this slice need no contract.
TESTS: each test at the lowest level that fails when the behavior breaks (unit, integration against the real dependency through the repo's existing harness, API/contract, architecture; E2E only for primary journeys); no sleeps, real clocks, unrecorded seeds, real external services, shared mutable state or assertions that cannot fail where they would hide or fake a regression; a new test framework, library or fixture only when requested, except a needed accessibility checker or real-dependency integration harness, justified as a dependency per `engineering-criteria` License stability (platform or first-party first, then a permissive or weak-copyleft, community-governed component; a single-vendor one only when none fits, with the reason recorded; a source-available, commercial or already-moved one only with user approval, so report it); a new expensive tier (E2E, load, mutation, suites over about 10 minutes) gets manual-dispatch CI only. Source: `engineering-criteria` Tests. Smoke suites and integration tiers that reach real network or cloud services follow `engineering-criteria` Resilience; unit tests still use no real external services.
Complete the scope, nothing else. Report pre-existing concerns unless required for this change. Resolve ambiguity from wording and surrounding code; state assumptions. Follow repo test patterns; leave a runnable check for each non-trivial branch or parser.
TOOLING: <shell to use; "a hook rewrites commands through rtk, do not hand-prefix" | "no rtk">. Use native tools for files, targeted reads and surgical edits. MCP/CLIs for this slice: <list>.
GATE: narrowest behavior check. Report command/result, failures and anything that cannot run/why; a failed start or syntax-only substitute is not a pass. No extra review/hardening or reviewer subagents; the orchestrator schedules review.
BRANCH: only <worktree>/<branch>. Commit completed items/resumable checkpoints with plain messages; never merge, push to the default branch or touch another checkout.
STATE: <absolute state path, or isolated relative path resolved against worktree root>.
HANDOFF: create <state>/handoff.md before investigation; update after commits/blockers and before reporting: scope, branch/worktree/worker id, commits, decisions, verification, blockers and exact next action.
CODEX ONLY: replace the BRANCH line with "BRANCH: only <worktree>; leave changes uncommitted; the orchestrator commits." and in HANDOFF/REPORT read "commits" as "changed files".
REPORT: at most about 30 lines covering the whole slice: changes/why, files, actual checks, decisions, risks and last commit. Tool-backed claims only; mark unverified. No transcripts/full diffs.
```

## Feedback loop (orchestrator)

1. Read the completion report and the real diff, not just the self-report. Done means diff reviewed and narrow checks green; update the slice table immediately. Fold every pre-existing concern a worker reports in this repository, related to the task or not, into the run as a slice or queue entry, except outside a scope the user narrowed, in a run adopted from `full-review` (held weaknesses the plan omits may sit near the code), in an unattended run, or in another repository: those go to the user in the final report, or through its caller when unattended. Doc gaps beyond the changed members and their containing type's own declaration are not folded in unless the user scoped doc work. A security or data-exposure defect goes only to the user (through its caller when unattended), never into a tracked file, commit, PR, issue or comment text, until the user decides how it is fixed. Defer only work too complex for the session, with the reason. A "needs contract" report: extend the design record (writing one if the run has none; one design lens pass on the change), marking the contract reuse, extend or new as in Phase 1 step 2; a mechanism slice the waiting slices depend on (never reopening a merged mechanism slice) extends or builds it, or for one reused as is adds only what the repo lacks of the architecture tests and of the end-to-end path for it. When a slice runs, bring its commits into each waiting slice's branch (merge default once it merges, keeping the worker's commits and taking the mechanism code from default on conflict) and send the worker the new contract with that commit; with no slice (a reused mechanism that lacks neither), first bring default into each waiting slice's branch that lacks that mechanism or its tests (same merge rule), then send the worker the contract, with that commit when one was made. In a run executing a handed `full-review` plan, the slice stops and goes to the user instead of re-planning; slices that depend on it stay queued.
2. Send corrections to the same worker (SendMessage, or Codex resume) with a phase excerpt, handoff and diff. First confirm its worktree still exists; never resume into a removed worktree, since the worker may fall back into the primary checkout. Respawn only if unreachable or the worktree is gone.
3. Usage-limit or auth errors are not failures to retry: queue the slice for that family's reset or route it to another eligible family, and record it. Mechanical failure: one same-config retry with the primary error. Reasoning failure: re-dispatch one tier up (haiku -> sonnet -> opus -> fable unless banned; Codex medium -> high, then stop). At the top eligible model, stop with evidence. At most two escalations.
4. Open items without a blocker get a concrete continue, not a respawn. After two continues treat as reasoning failure. Background commands/agents still running mean not done.
5. For long slices schedule a fresh verifier against SCOPE. Read only relevant errors/bounded log tails on failure.

## Review path

Every lens gets fresh context, an immutable diff and read access, never the authoring conversation; it reports only. `<review>` = `<root>/.tmp/orchestrated-refactor/<run-id>/review/`. Inputs go in `<review>/in/`, reports in `<review>/out/review-<short-sha>-<lens>-<n>.md` (check absent first; never overwrite a live one). Freeze inputs with `git diff --output="<review>/in/<sha>.diff" <base>...<head>` (delta: `git diff --output="<review>/in/<sha>-delta.diff" <prev-head>..<head>`) and review from `git worktree add --detach "<root>/.tmp/worktrees/<run-id>-review-<short-sha>" <head>`; remove that checkout once its last reviewer ends.

Classes: risky = security, money, migration, infrastructure, dependency or agent-policy (instructions, skills, scripts). Logic-bearing = any other diff that changes a branch, loop, parser, state, cleanup or error path, or a value other code reads. Trivial = non-risky wording, comments, formatting or inert data. Exempt only prose-only docs or typo/comment fixes; record the exemption.

Severity: HIGH = data loss, security exposure or broken primary path in a realistic scenario; MEDIUM = wrong behavior in a realistic secondary scenario; LOW = edge cases, wording, docs, style. Every finding needs file:line and a concrete failure scenario.

Reviewer forms (run from the review checkout, in background, in parallel):
- Claude: `claude -p "$(cat "<prompt-file>")" --model opus --tools "Read,Grep,Glob" --strict-mcp-config --permission-mode default --add-dir "<review>/in" > "<report>"`; the prompt file ends "Put your complete report in your final message; you cannot write files." Only if the CLI is unavailable, use an `Agent` general-purpose reviewer (no isolation) alone, and compare `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` of the checkouts before/after, since it is read-only only by prompt (writes to ignored paths go undetected).
- Codex (if detected): `codex exec --json -s read-only -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort=<low|medium|high by size/risk> -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=230000 -c model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope=total -C "<checkout>" --output-last-message "<report>" "$(cat "<prompt-file>")" < /dev/null > "<report-stem>.jsonl"`. No `--add-dir` (it grants writes); name the diff path in the prompt.
- Success: exit 0 and a nonempty report ending in a coverage line (sweep) or verdict (intent, delta). On failure read the primary error and retry once; a usage-limit/auth error or second failure records the lens unavailable for that head, never clean.

Prompts:
- Intent: diff, PR intent and claims. Ask for bugs, security issues, missed edge cases, unintended changes, and whether the design holds (claims vs behavior, guards weakened, callers and scope missed). Ends with a verdict.
- Unanchored sweep (no intent): "Report-only line-by-line sweep of <diff> in <checkout>. Judge behavior against the code's own claims. Read every hunk and its dependencies; check A-J; search every removed/renamed identifier. One finding per line: [class] SEVERITY file:line - defect. Scenario: input/state -> wrong outcome. End with files covered/total." Checklist: A atomicity/races; B comments, docs or messages that describe behavior the code lacks; C parity between things that must match (prod/test hosts, config/defaults, write/read validation); D leftovers of removed identifiers; E exception paths (pass E below verbatim); F null/empty/zero/overflow/culture/missing-config inputs; G disposal and unbounded growth; H vacuous tests, or new non-trivial logic with no check that would fail; I secrets, authz bypass, injection; J code no requirement needs, or a second implementation of a mechanism the repo or design record already has (a lock, idempotency-key format, notification path or cache eviction) (resilience at network and cloud boundaries and scale work required by `engineering-criteria` Scale are not needless).
  - **E. Exception paths.** Swallowed failures. A catch/finally throw replacing the original exception. Retries or fallbacks masking an undiagnosed failure or spending their budget on the wrong error. Missing standard resilience; unproven `RemoveAllResilienceHandlers`, disabled SDK retries, `MaxRetries = 0`, custom pipelines or, for transient faults, "next run retries" (`engineering-criteria` Resilience). `RemoveAllResilienceHandlers()` immediately followed by `AddStandardResilienceHandler(o => ...)` that keeps unsafe-method retries off (or, for a keyed client, sets the keyed `Retry.ShouldHandle`; `engineering-criteria` Resilience) is correct for a defaults-inherited options override; flag removal without such a re-add unless its site comment gives a proven reason that `engineering-criteria` allows. Disabling SDK retries for a known non-idempotent, unkeyed operation when the server offers no idempotency key, with a one-line site reason, is correct. The documented shared-helper pattern with cmdlet, curl or github-script built-in retries off and one helper retrying for idempotent calls is also correct.
- Delta: the delta diff, current full diff, checkout and the findings being fixed. Read every changed block and its callers; verify each fix and ask what it broke (cleanup paths, error handling, test isolation, defaults other callers reach, docs made untrue). Ends with a verdict.

Rounds:
- Round 1 before PR, in parallel on full `base...head`: opus intent plus opus unanchored sweep. Risky and logic-bearing diffs add a cross-family unanchored sweep from the family that did not author it: Codex on Claude-authored work if detected. On all-Codex authorship the Claude lenses are already cross-family; record that. Mixed authorship or the other family unavailable: record cross-family unavailable; same-family lenses gate. On a risky or logic-bearing diff with no separate cross-family sweep, add a sonnet second sweep.
- Verify and deduplicate every finding against the code, LOW/nits included; fix as one set or rebut with evidence (cite the type, caller or guard). A finding whose cause is in the approach is fixed by refactoring the approach in that set, not by a patch per symptom. Send fixes to the owning worker while its worktree exists, otherwise a new worker/branch from default.
- Round 1 fixes that change logic (LOW-only included) get one delta; fixes that are only code comments or human-facing docs do not (in agent instructions and skills, wording is logic). Another delta only after a confirmed HIGH/MEDIUM in the preceding delta. A fix set that replaces an approach gets its delta plus a full unanchored sweep, counted together as one delta. Cap: round 1 plus 2 deltas (3 for integrated diffs over about 2,000 changed lines) per cycle.
- Merge-head pass, outside the cap, at most once per review cycle: if logic changed after round 1, run one orchestrator-family full unanchored sweep of the final head, plus a cross-family sweep, when available and the orchestrator family is not already cross-family to every author, on a risky PR or a logic-bearing PR where a cross-family lens raised a confirmed HIGH/MEDIUM. HIGH/MEDIUM from it gets a delta, which counts as extra if the cap is spent.
- No PR merges with an open HIGH or MEDIUM, even past the cap. Deltas past the cap count as extra, the merge-head pass excluded. Two triggers: the design trigger is a HIGH/MEDIUM confirmed by the cap's last planned delta or any later review of cycle 1 (merge-head pass excluded; per area on a Large PR, below); the loop-safety trigger is a HIGH/MEDIUM confirmed by the second extra delta or any later review of a cycle, and ends that cycle. A cycle that ends with nothing open goes on to the merge gates. Every LOW and nit is fixed or explicitly rebutted.
- Redesign cycle, at most once per PR (once per area on a Large PR, below): when the design trigger fires, before the next fix set, a fresh-context opus design lens reads intent, any design record, the full diff and every round's findings and fixes, and returns `design` (the open findings share a cause in the approach, such as one invariant, data path, ownership or state model; it names the cause, a replacement design (any shared mechanism it needs marked per Phase 1 step 2) and any scope growth that design needs) or `not-design` (independent findings, reviewer churn or contested findings); a design lens unavailable after its retry counts as `not-design`. On `not-design`, the current cycle continues with extra deltas and the diagnosis is kept for any loop-safety report. On `design`, unless it cannot be taken here (next bullet), notify the user (cause, design, scope growth; push notification where available; an unattended run uses only its caller's channel) without waiting, record scope growth in SCOPE/DONE, the handoff and the PR body, dispatch the implementation to workers (unless quota/routing sends it elsewhere; a cause in a shared mechanism changes its design-record contract first), and start the next cycle (cycle 2 after the first redesign) on the new head: full round 1 with authorship and the risk class reassessed, a fresh cap, its own extra deltas and its own merge-head pass. Scope may grow when doing the original intent properly requires it (more files, a changed contract, a dependency or migration); a newly added risky class makes the PR risky from that cycle's round 1, and the merge confirmation rules still apply. A held security or data-exposure fix keeps the cause, design and growth out of the PR and tracked files (only in `.tmp/` review records and the final message); its notice says only that a redesign started.
- A `design` cannot be taken here when the redesign would change the intent or add separable work that belongs on its own branch, when an unattended run (no user present) would need scope growth or depart from an owner-approved specification's design, or when a run executing a handed `full-review` plan would need more than its slices' SCOPE and DONE (never re-planned here).
- Large PR (over about 2,000 changed lines): the round 1 of the first cycle in which it is that large records its areas in the review table (file groups, or the design record's lifecycles where one exists); later cycles keep them, and a redesign taken before counts toward the bound below. The design trigger, design lens and redesign cycle then apply per area: an area's design trigger is a HIGH/MEDIUM in that area confirmed by a cycle's last planned delta or any later review of that cycle (merge-head pass excluded), in any cycle before that area's redesign; its lens reads intent, any design record, that area's diff and every round's findings and fixes for it; each area gets at most one redesign. Areas that trigger on the same review each get their lens, and every `design` among them is implemented in one next cycle. At most three redesign cycles per PR; after the third, a design trigger counts as a loop-safety trigger. Every cycle's rounds still review the whole new head; the loop-safety trigger and stop apply to the whole PR.
- Loop-safety stop: when the loop-safety trigger ends any cycle, or a `design` cannot be taken here, stop. After a `design` that could not be taken here, a user approval of its reserved change or scope growth starts the next cycle as above (for a handed `full-review` plan, the approval is a `full-review` re-run, never growth in place, since held weaknesses may sit near the grown scope); separable work still goes on its own branch. Report the open findings, every cycle's fix history and the design lens's diagnosis to the user; merge waits for their decision (an unattended run applies its caller's needs-human signal instead).
- Record every round (cycle, head, lenses/models, findings, dispositions, unavailable lenses, fixes no reviewer read) in the PR body's review table and the tracked handoff.

## Integrate and merge

Only the orchestrator opens and merges PRs. For each PR (one per increment, Ship in increments below), integrate its slice branches onto one branch, run the full affected checks locally, and run Review path round 1 on the integrated diff (slice checks never substitute). Then `git push -u origin <branch>` and open that PR (via `gh` if detected) stating what, why, validation and the review table; later rounds follow on the PR. Before merge, audit the full `base...head`: intended scope only, no secrets or stray artifacts (`.tmp/`, test output, logs), no unintended dependency, lockfile, migration, CI workflow or infrastructure change; record the audit in the PR. Merge only with local checks passing, required CI green, review done/exempt with no open HIGH/MEDIUM, and the audit clean. Never push to the default branch directly or force-push shared branches. Confirm with the user before any merge that deploys, publishes, migrates data or changes credentials. If Graphify was detected and the change is material, offer a graph refresh as its own commit.

Ship in increments: work larger than one reviewable PR (about 2,000 changed lines) ships as several PRs in dependency order, the mechanism slices (slice 0 and any split of it) first, each merged to default behind the feature's rollout flag (the repo's existing config or flag provider, never a new one without approval, and a removal plan) or, for a refactor, each leaving default working; never one long-lived branch. Each PR's integrated diff gets its own Review path; later slices branch from default after the PRs they depend on merge. A handed `full-review` plan keeps its PR grouping; a grouped PR over about 2,000 changed lines takes the larger cap (Review path) and the Large PR rule.

After each verified merge, preserve useful worker decisions in the tracked handoff. Stop the dev servers, watchers, test hosts, build servers and background shells that PR's slices and reviews started before removing those slices' clean worktrees, branches and state and that PR's review checkouts, so nothing holds a file handle; other slices, and entries kept for the user's decision, stay. At run end remove run scratch and confirm no run worktrees, branches or state remain except those kept for the user's decision, listed in the handoff. Leave every entry outside this run's slice table and review checkouts alone.

## Session handoff

Before ending, update active count, queue, slices, paths, decisions, checks, Environment table and exact next action. List every deliberately kept worktree/state/review input. Never unlock, remove or reuse another session's entries. A later session resumes from the tracked handoff alone; replacement workers use their own handoff and last commit.

## Token discipline

- Prefer a few complete slices to tiny spawns.
- Scope and retrieve better instead of raising tier/effort for long prompts.
- Read completion reports and diffs, never full transcripts or JSONL logs.
